messages.subject: Maximum dataset size
messages.body_plain:
Dear Listserve,

I have a question regarding maximum dataset size in MatchIt. I am trying to run

m.out<-matchit(Treated ~ X1 + X2 + X3 + X4 + X5, data = lucas, method = "optimal", distance = "mahalanobis", ratio=2)

but receive the following error message

Error in matrix(0, ncol = N0, nrow = n1) : too many elements specified

The
dataset is 10 columns wide and 466285 rows long. A big matrix, but I'm
dealing with landscape level issues, trying to determine deforestation impacts and control for physiographic covariates. Of the 466285 entries, 112239 are "treated".

I know this code works because when I run it on smaller datasets it goes no problem.

Can anyone tell me if there is a maximum matrix size using MatchIt, and if so, any potential workaround solutions to this issue?

Thanks so much for your help.

Cheers,

Lucas Joppa
 * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

messages.subject: Re: Maximum dataset size
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

   If you are a Windows user, check out: 
http://gking.harvard.edu/zelig/docs/static/faq.pdf

   If you are a Mac/Linux user, you need to install 64 bit version of R. 
See http://r.research.att.com/exp/

   Another solution is to split the data according to the discrete 
covariates on which you can exactly match.  Then, within each of those 
subsets of the data, you can perform matching.

Best,
Kosuke

messages.subject: Re: Maximum dataset size
messages.body_plain:
Kosuke's last suggestion is close to CEM which works within matchit.  
the original CEM program (at my web site) is somewhat more efficient for 
very large data sets (by dropping some of the nice front end of 
matchit).  If you use eval=FALSE in the call to cem, it should work with 
any data set size, subject to how much memory you have available.
Gary

messages.subject: how to combine matching and survey weights
messages.subject_clean: how to combine matching and survey weights
messages.body_plain:
Hey all-

I have some county-level exit poll data I am using with full matching.
But, since they are exit poll data, I also have to apply a weight to
correct for non-random sampling (this weight is based on county-level
turnout data on race, gender, age, vote share, etc...). Can I just
multiply the survey and matching weights together to get a summary
weight, or is it more complicated than this?

Thanks much,

-c

-- 
Casey A. Klofstad
University of Miami
Department of Political Science
Coral Gables, FL

messages.subject: Re: how to combine matching and survey weights
messages.subject_clean: how to combine matching and survey weights
messages.body_plain:
sorry about that. i hit send accidentally.  here's the full version:

Hi Casey, there are other approaches, but I'd ignore the sampling 
weights for estimating causal effects.  As long as you condition (in 
this case match) on the survey weights or (better) the variables that 
compose the survey weights, you're not going to have any bias.  Note, 
however, that the goal of matching is to find a subset of units for 
which you can estimate a casual effect reasonably reliably and that 
subsample may not be the one you're after; of course any other subsample 
may produce inferences that are so model dependent that it would be 
uninformative.  This by the way is no different from linear regression, 
where you'd control for the survey weights as pre-treatment control 
variables.

Best,
Gary
---
http://gking.harvard.edu

messages.subject_clean: how to combine matching and survey weights
messages.body_plain:
If you have a good estimate for each pair/subclass (or more genreally if 
the ATE varies as a function of pre-treatment covariates X) then you might 
be able to wait each pair according to the sampling weights to recover the 
population ATE as:

\sum ATE(x) w(x)/\sum w(x)

Kosuke

-- 
Department of Politics
Princeton University
http://imai.princeton.edu

messages.subject: variable length error with "weights"
messages.body_plain:
Hey all-

I posted the below onthe Zelig discussion board, but I think this
might also be related to MatchIt:

I just weighted some data, and am trying to examine the results with
ordered logit. The code is:

z.out <- zelig(as.factor(polact) ~ treat, weights="weights", data =
mi(ds1, ds2, ds3, ds4, ds5), model = "ologit")

This produces the error:

Error in model.frame.default(formula = as.factor(polact) ~ treat, data = list( :
variable lengths differ (found for '(weights)')

The same weighted model above runs fine in OLS, and I am running
MatchIt Version 2.4-10 (downloaded from Gary King's website).

Thoughts?

Thanks much,

-c

-- 
Casey A. Klofstad
University of Miami
Department of Political Science
Coral Gables, FL

klofstad-Re5JQEeQqe8AvxtiuMwx3w at public.gmane.org
